dialect.detail: Likely a Brazilian microcomputer COBOL environment (possibly Micro Focus or a local vendor like Unimake/Datasul era), using SCREEN SECTION with BCK-CLR/FOR-CLR attributes, GOBACK, LINKAGE SECTION with PRM-OPR, and calls to proprietary routines DYSPOL/DYMSGM/DYHELP/DYIMPR. Portuguese-language identifiers and Brazilian CEP (postal code) handling. DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA is typical for Brazilian Portuguese locale.
evidence: Portuguese identifiers: NOM-MDR, END-MDR, CID-MDR, EST-MDR

purpose.domain_detail: Brazilian customer mailing-label (mala-direta) system — generates address labels for a customer master file range
purpose.summary: Program DY3230 is a batch/interactive program that reads a range of customer records from an indexed master file (CADMDR), formats mailing-label data (name, address, CEP/city/state), writes them to a temporary indexed file (CADTMP), and then calls a print routine (DYIMPR) to produce the physical labels. It provides a screen-based UI for entering the start/end customer code range and displays page count progress.

notable_features: SCREEN SECTION with BCK-CLR/FOR-CLR color attributes and box-drawing characters
LINKAGE SECTION with PROCEDURE DIVISION USING (called as subprogram)
Calls to proprietary framework routines: DYSPOL, DYMSGM, DYHELP, DYIMPR
INDEXED files with DYNAMIC access and FILE STATUS
ACCEPT ... FROM ESCAPE KEY for function-key handling
Portuguese-language variable names and screen text
verdict.notes: File decoded as latin-1; screen section contains extended IBM PC box-drawing characters (Û, É, º, È, etc.) consistent with a DOS/Brazilian microcomputer COBOL environment. No COMP-3 usage. The DY prefix on program and called routines suggests a proprietary application framework. Cannot determine exact compiler/vendor without more context.
